title: Firmware Faults
description: Firmware scenario analysis (sc arc): fault kinds as objects (one class per kind: concurrency, physical triggers, space/safety), the assumptions they break, the techniques that restore them with their measured cost, and scenarios forced on the UNO twin at an exact PC — BEFORE fails at a named cycle, AFTER holds — each run a witness or counterexample written as a mathproofs claim; sc-2: the statistics tier as campaigns (the fault's rate as the stimulus → likelihood per fault kind with Wilson intervals); sc-2b: CBMC FormalChecks (decided (bounded) / refuted with a trace / inapplicable) and cppcheck rules per variant; sc-2c: Frama-C/Mthread race checks (decided (unbounded) / refuted with the two racing lines) beside CBMC's. sc-3: the RTOS pairs on the ESP32-C3 QEMU twin.

engines.name: avr-twin
engines.note: the simavr UNO twin WITH the scenario flags — sc-0 (prf-board-engines/twin_forcing.c: --irq-at pc=/cycle=, --poke, --watch, --trace-vcd, --sp-watch, --stack-fill, --isr-latency, --fn-cycles, --uart-out, --seed) and sc-1 (twin_scenario_io.c: --inject, --respond, --drop-frame rx:N, --uart-ber, --rx-noise, --reset-at, --jump-at, --eeprom-set/-dump, --uart-tx-log/-rx-log; twin_forcing.c: --ret-hist/--ret-log, ISR lengths, --fn-cycles START:ret) and sc-2 (--align-at-pc, --flip-bit, --drop-frame tx:N[,type=] / rx:p=P, 64 --irq-at) — resolved through the BOARD engines seam (board.custom.board_engines: BOARD_ENGINES_URL → local binary → the local image prf-board-engines:trixie → topology provider board.engines → refusal)

engines.name: avr-gcc
engines.note: builds the scenario variants (board.custom.build) and the static stack peak: -fstack-usage + -fcallgraph-info=su (GCC's own .su/.ci; avstack.pl is NOT vendored)

engines.name: avr-objdump
engines.note: binutils-avr: the disassembly every step re-resolves its PC against (the lds sequence of g_ms in hal_millis); avr-nm for the symbol table — both in prf-board-engines, run through the same seam (firmwarefaults.custom.fault_engines)

engines.name: pyvcd
engines.note: pyvcd 0.5.0 (MIT) installed by sha256 in prf-board-engines; polari-vcd-window reads the twin's VCD into the cycles-around-the-fault rows ENGINE-side (not a framework library)

engines.name: cbmc
engines.note: sc-2b: CBMC 6.6.0 (Debian trixie; BSD-4-clause style — an advertising clause, so GPL-incompatible to LINK: run ONLY as a separate-process engine) in its own worker image prf-formal-engines:trixie (goto-cc → goto-instrument → cbmc, driven by polari-cbmc-check) — resolved through the FORMAL engines seam (firmwarefaults.custom.formal_engines: FORMAL_ENGINES_URL → local binary → the local image prf-formal-engines:trixie → topology provider firmwarefaults.formal → refusal naming the knob)

engines.name: cppcheck
engines.note: sc-2b: cppcheck 2.17.1 (GPL-3.0) in the same image — built-in checks + the threadsafety addon on every firmware variant; the MISRA addon is NOT run (its rule texts need the non-free MISRA C document); findings are rows, never a build failure

engines.name: frama-c-mthread
engines.note: sc-2c: Frama-C 33.0 (Arsenic) + its Mthread plugin (LGPL-2.1-only; Debian has no frama-c package, so an opam build pinned to an opam-repository commit, runtime closure only) in the SAME image prf-formal-engines:trixie (+185 MB, under the ~1.5 GB fold-in line); no SMT prover wired (WP not used; never Alt-Ergo's NC build — the free alt-ergo-free is what frama-c's opam requires); resolved through the same FORMAL engines seam (FORMAL_ENGINES_URL → local binary → the local image when its org.polari.engines label lists mthread-check → topology provider firmwarefaults.formal → refusal naming the knob)

engines.name: c3-run
engines.note: sc-3: the ESP32-C3 twin for the RTOS scenarios — Espressif QEMU fork esp_develop_9.2.2_20260417 (GPL-2.0-only, -machine esp32c3, -icount 3) driven by polari-c3-run, and ESP-IDF v5.5.5 (polari-idf-build) for the C3 variants, both in prf-esp-engines:noble — resolved through the BOARD engines seam's esp family (ESP_ENGINES_URL → local binary → the local image prf-esp-engines:noble → topology provider board.esp-engines → refusal)

requires.engines_note: the twin and the AVR toolchain resolve through the board engines seam (the same knob, image and provider as board); CBMC and cppcheck through the formal engines seam (FORMAL_ENGINES_URL, prf-formal-engines:trixie, firmwarefaults.formal); Frama-C/Mthread through the same seam (mthread-check in the same image); nothing runs in the framework process except the parsing
